summary: Sanity checks confirm GRASP is a graph-based model that ignores stereochemistry and input token aromaticity labels, relying on learned connectivity.

claims.test: MolFromSmiles('CCO') -> canonical vs random SMILES. CosineDist(CLS_canonical, CLS_random) < 1e-6.
claims.prediction: Distance should be ~0.0 for graph models; >0.1 implies string dependency.
Distance should be ~0.0; >0.5 implies stereo encoding.

claims.claim: Pretrained weights are stable; random init explodes (Inf norms).
claims.test: MolFromSmiles('CCO'). Layer-12 norm < 50 for pretrained; > 100 or Inf for random.
claims.prediction: Pretrained norms should be stable (<50); Random norms unstable (>100) without training.

claims.claim: Input tokens do not fully encode aromaticity (48.6% mixed).
claims.test: MolFromSmiles('c1ccccc1') vs MolFromSmiles('C1=CC=CC=C1'). Check token ID for C atoms.
claims.prediction: If tokens differ, aromaticity is encoded in input; if same, model must learn it.

claims.claim: Pretrained CLS uses more dimensions (Effective Rank 9.89 vs 5.81).
claims.test: Compute covariance eigenvalues of CLS layer-12 over 'mols' set.
claims.prediction: Pretrained rank > Random rank indicates better feature utilization.

trivial_explanations: SMILES invariance is expected for graph models (RDKit canonicalization vs random permutation).
Stereo blindness is expected if input lacks chiral tags or model architecture ignores them.
Inf norms in random init indicate divergence without gradient descent regularization.
